name: Gunnamatta Ocean Beach
signature: The Peninsula's most powerful surf beach — raw Bass Strait swell, dramatic dunes, and patrolled in summer by Gunnamatta SLSC
editorNote:
Gunnamatta is the Peninsula's most serious surf beach — a long exposed stretch of Bass Strait coastline where the swell arrives uninterrupted from Antarctica. The beach breaks are powerful and shifty, the rips are strong, and on a good day it produces the best surf on the Peninsula. It is not a beginner beach.

The dunes behind the beach are significant — part of the Peninsula's coastal heathland — and the walk from the car park delivers one of those first-glimpse moments that stops people mid-stride. Even non-surfers come here for the view, the walk along the beach, and the sheer scale of the ocean.

Patrolled by Gunnamatta SLSC on weekends and public holidays from late November through Easter. Always swim between the flags. Check Swellnet or Willyweather before you go — the difference between a fun 2ft beach break and a dangerous close-out can be a single metre of swell.
whyWeGo: Gunnamatta is the Peninsula's most powerful surf beach — raw Bass Strait swell and dramatic dunes that make every other beach feel tame.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk to the top of the dunes before you hit the beach. The first view of the ocean stops you every time.
